title: B200: add smoke suite (minimal workloads + sanity thresholds) [allowed-to-fail]
author: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Context: We’re starting to bring up early B200 nodes and need a minimal benchmark-lab signal that (a) the runner can successfully execute end-to-end on B200, (b) latency/throughput aren’t obviously broken (e.g., kernel fallbacks everywhere, allocator thrash, pathological queueing), and (c) results are persisted/tagged by profile_version + git SHA for triage. This PR adds a B200 smoke suite with a very small matrix and coarse “sanity thresholds”. The suite is intentionally marked allowed-to-fail initially (non-blocking) while Infra standardizes driver/CUDA baselines and Runtime finalizes provisional profiles. Tracking: ENG-4928 (bring-up checklist) / ENG-4929 (CI integration).

What’s included: Adds a new suite `b200_smoke` with 3 minimal workloads covering prefill-heavy, decode-heavy, and mixed. Introduces conservative pass/fail criteria: hard failures for runner crashes, repeated OOM, and extreme regression bands; warnings for borderline perf, high kernel fallback, or high variance. Adds tagging/metadata for results: `gpu_sku=b200`, `profile_version` (if provided), `cuda_driver`, and `runner_git_sha`. Integrates the suite into the existing CI workflow as non-blocking (allowed-to-fail) with a dedicated check name so we can trend it without stopping merges.

Workloads (minimal matrix): 1) short prefill + short decode (sanity for fast path), 2) long-ish prefill + short decode (KV/prefill pressure), 3) mixed prompt lengths at low concurrency (basic scheduler behavior). Model set mirrors existing smoke philosophy: small-ish open model variant already in our runner images + one “serving-like” model used in other suites when available. Note: exact model artifacts still come from the standard benchmark-lab cache; no new large model downloads are required by this change.

Sanity thresholds (initial): These are intentionally loose and framed as guardrails, not targets. Current behavior in early B200 nodes is noisy due to driver/CUDA variance and runtime kernel fallback conditions. Thresholds are expressed as (1) must-not-happen events (crash/OOM), and (2) coarse bounds on p95 latency and tokens/sec relative to the prior run on the same host label when available, otherwise a static ceiling/floor. We also emit a “suspicious” warning if kernel_fallback_rate > 5% on any workload bucket.

Allowed-to-fail semantics: CI will surface the check result and upload artifacts, but will not block merges. The check is configured to fail the job only for infra-level errors (runner exception, missing GPU, artifact upload failure). Benchmark-level failures are recorded in the summary and posted as a warning annotation.

Notes / follow-ups: Once Infra’s B200 baseline is stable and the runtime profile compatibility gate is in place everywhere, we should flip this to blocking and tighten thresholds (see ENG-4928). Also expected to update the suite to read profile pack version pins from the runner env when runtime-1.22 lands broadly.

Checklist: - [x] Suite definition + runner integration - [x] Results tagging includes sku/profile_version/driver - [x] CI check added as non-blocking - [x] Artifacts uploaded (json + summary) - [x] Docs: short README section explaining allowed-to-fail and how to run locally
commits: bench/suites: add b200_smoke suite definition + workloads
runner: plumb gpu_sku + cuda_driver metadata into result envelope
ci: add b200 smoke check (allowed-to-fail) + artifact upload
docs: add instructions for running b200_smoke locally
conversation: Claire Dubois: Thresholds look reasonable as a starting point. Can we make the “relative to prior run” logic explicitly fallback to static only when no baseline is found, and log which path we took?
Rina Kobayashi (author): Yep — added an explicit summary line “threshold_mode=relative|static” per workload and included the baseline id when present.
Irene Choi: Please ensure we capture driver/CUDA versions in the result envelope. We’ve seen mismatches on the early nodes and need to correlate quickly.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added `cuda_driver` and `cuda_runtime` fields from nvidia-smi + runtime query; included in tags and in the summary header.
Sahana Iyer: CI semantics: I’m worried about accidentally making this blocking later. Can we isolate it into its own check name and make the workflow annotation explicit about non-blocking?

Rina Kobayashi (author): Done — check name is `bench: b200_smoke (allowed-to-fail)` and the summary includes a banner. The workflow uses continue-on-error for the benchmark step but still fails on runner/infra errors.
Jonas Weber: Can we add a guardrail for kernel fallback rate? Even if loose, a warning would be useful for bring-up.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added `kernel_fallback_rate` warning threshold at 5% (warning only). Hard fail still limited to crash/OOM/infra errors for now.
Claire Dubois: Approved after the threshold_mode logging change.
Sahana Iyer: Approved. Please link this PR in ENG-4928 so we remember to flip to blocking later.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Linked in Linear and added a follow-up note in docs/ci.md.
release_notes:
- Added B200 smoke suite (non-blocking) with minimal workloads and sanity thresholds
- Result metadata now includes gpu_sku/profile_version/cuda driver info for triage
